Living Well / Free resources

Files, sharing & recovery

A useful way in

Choose one place to begin.

Move a file, keep a working copy current, or plan for recovery without confusing those three purposes.

Convenience and recoverability are different goals. This collection distinguishes nearby transfer, synchronization, backup, password management, collaborative storage, and account exports. Choose the smallest appropriate system and understand the responsibilities that come with it.

Start with: LocalSend: move a file nearby. Use the native apps, confirm the receiving device, and transfer a harmless sample first.

Resources with a clear purpose.

Nearby file transfer · Free core app

LocalSend: move a file nearby

LocalSend project

Move an approved file between nearby devices without making a cloud account part of that task.

Begin here: Use the native apps, confirm the receiving device, and transfer a harmless sample first.

Access: Free open-source native apps on supported desktop and mobile platforms. Install on both devices and use a working local network.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open LocalSend: move a file nearby

Context & source

This selection concerns native local-network transfer, not every web mode. A transferred copy is not automatic synchronization or a backup strategy.

File synchronization · Free core app

Syncthing: keep selected folders aligned

Syncthing project

An option for keeping a deliberately chosen folder current across computers you control.

Begin here: Read the getting-started guide and test with a new folder containing expendable files.

Access: Free open-source software; supported devices must be configured to communicate. Network and platform requirements apply.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open Syncthing: keep selected folders aligned

Context & source

Its own FAQ warns that edits and deletions propagate and that synchronization is not a sufficient backup. Keep separate recovery copies.

Folder comparison · Free core app

FreeFileSync: compare folders first

FreeFileSync project

See differences between two folders before deciding what should be copied or updated.

Begin here: Read the tutorial for the intended sync mode and preview changes on a small test folder.

Access: Free for personal home use; business use requires a separate license. Storage devices and optional editions have their own costs.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open FreeFileSync: compare folders first

Context & source

Mirror, update, and two-way behavior differ. A wrong direction can delete files; a completed copy operation does not prove recoverability.

Backup documentation · Free to browse

Duplicati: plan a recoverable backup

Duplicati project

A route into configuring a backup with a deliberate destination and a tested restore, rather than merely accumulating copies.

Begin here: Begin with the official setup guide, back up harmless sample files, and learn how to restore them.

Access: Free public documentation for the open-source client. Storage destinations and optional managed services can have costs and account requirements.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open Duplicati: plan a recoverable backup

Context & source

Preserve recovery credentials securely and test restoration before relying on a backup. This is documentation review, not a security or reliability test.

Password management · Free core app

KeePassXC: a local password database

KeePassXC team

Consider a locally managed database when you are willing to take responsibility for its access and recovery.

Begin here: Read the official getting-started material before changing how important accounts are managed.

Access: Free open-source desktop software for supported Windows, macOS, and Linux systems; no cloud account is required for its core use.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open KeePassXC: a local password database

Context & source

Protect the database and its unlock method and maintain safe recovery copies. Local control does not eliminate phishing, device compromise, or forgotten-credential risks.

Password management · Free account for participation

Bitwarden: a free personal vault

Bitwarden

A cross-device option to compare with a locally managed database or a password manager you already use.

Begin here: Choose the free personal plan and read its setup and recovery documentation before importing important data.

Access: A free account provides core personal password management. Premium features, family plans, and some sharing functions cost extra.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open Bitwarden: a free personal vault

Context & source

Keep recovery information safe and understand which features your plan includes. Directory inclusion is not a security guarantee or an instruction to share credentials here.

CryptPad: collaborative documents

CryptPad project

Examine document ownership and access before choosing a shared writing space for a small group.

Begin here: Read the account and document-ownership guidance, then agree which host and access model the group will use.

Google Takeout: keep an export

Google

Begin here: Read the product-specific options and export a small, suitable selection first.

Backup guide · Free to browse

Time Machine: a Mac backup

Apple

An existing operating-system feature to examine before adding a new backup subscription.

Begin here: Read the storage requirements and learn both backup setup and file restoration.

Access: Free instructions and a feature included with compatible macOS systems; suitable separate storage is required and may cost money.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Confirm the intended disk and protect existing files before setup. A backup should be checked through a harmless restore, not just a reassuring status message.
